 Judgment

1. This appeal is directed against the order of Ld. Trial Court dated 06.09.2023, passed in the matter titled as 'Smt. Shabnam Mohd. Kalam & Ors Vs. Smt. Shabnam Taranum Page no.1 of 5. Taranum Vs. Mohd. Asif and Ors.' bearing no. 1196/2023, because by the said order, the appellants were summoned as a respondents in the said case.

2. Shorn of unnecessary details, alleged facts of the case are that on 26.06.2007, the respondent was married to one Mohd. Asif i.e., the son of appellant no.1 and 2 and the brother of appellant no.3.
After the marriage, the respondent was taken to her matrimonial home.
Three children were born out of the wedlock.

However, the appellants used to constantly harass and torture the respondent Mohd. Kalam vs Smt. Shabnam Taranum on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59417685/
1 for not bringing sufficient dowry.

entities.text: Mohd. Kalam vs Smt. Shabnam Taranum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They used to harass and torture her for bringing more money from her parents and also used to threaten her that she would not be allowed to stay at her matrimonial home, if she failed to comply.
They also used to beat her for bringing money from her parents.
The appellants also misappropriated the 'streedhan' of the respondent which were given to them.

Later,
her husband solemnized second marriage on 14.07.2016.
Thereafter, on 10.08.2016, the respondent was driven out of her matrimonial home along with her two children.

After the second marriage of his brother, appellant no.3 used to tell the respondent that after the said second marriage, the respondent and her children had no concern with them and there was not nothing left for them in her matrimonial house.

3. It was argued by the counsel for appellants that the respondent had lodged an FIR No. 734/2016,
under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, PS Jaitpur, on the basis of same allegations as levelled in her complaint, in which the husband of the respondent namely Mohd. Asif and his parents i.e. appellant no.1 and 2 Mohd. Kalam & Ors Vs. Smt. Shabnam Taranum Page no.2 of 5. herein, were acquitted.

entities.text: Mohd. Kalam & Ors Vs. Smt. Shabnam Taranum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the said fact has been concealed by the respondent in her complaint before Ld. Trial Court.
He argued that once appellant no.1 and 2 have been acquitted in the aforesaid case based on the same allegations, the appellants herein can not be summoned by the Ld. Trial Court.
4. Per contra, counsel for the respondent argued that in the said case bearing FIR No. 734/2016, PS Jaitpur, appellant no.3 was not an accused.

Moreover, even if the accused persons are acquitted of an offence punishable under Indian Penal Code, the same does not bar a proceeding under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as 'Act').

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In support of his arguments, counsel for the appellant relied on the following judgments:
a) Hardeep Khan Vs. Rano, CRM-M No. 44742/2021 (Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court)
b) Chandan Kumar Sahoo & Ors. Vs. Putul Sahoo, Cr. Rev No. 2981/2018 (Hon'ble Calcutta High Court)
5.

entities.text: Hardeep Khan Vs. Rano, CRM-M No. 44742/2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Chandan Kumar Sahoo & Ors. Vs. Putul Sahoo, Cr. Rev No. 2981/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments and have gone through the Ld. Trial Court record including the case laws relied on.

6. In Hardeep Khan (supra), it was held that for conviction of an offender under Section 498A of IPC i.e., a criminal case, charges are to be proved by the prosecution beyond the shadows of reasonable doubt and the Court has to follow the procedure as prescribed under Cr.P.C and Evidence Act.
However, the application under the Act is of different nature.

The intent of Legislature is to provide protection to a lady who is suffering Mohd. Kalam & Ors Vs. Smt. Shabnam Taranum Page no.3 of 5.
domestic violence in the hands of her husband or any member of matrimonial home.

entities.text: Mohd. Kalam & Ors Vs. Smt. Shabnam Taranum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant can claim various reliefs by filing such complaint like maintenance allowance, rent for separate accommodation, damages and compensation etc.
Therefore, more or less by filing application under Section 12 of the Act, the aggrieved person can get various reliefs by filing one application.

Mohd. Kalam vs Smt. Shabnam Taranum on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59417685/
2

entities.text: Mohd. Kalam vs Smt. Shabnam Taranum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also held that the proceedings under Section 12 of the Act and the proceedings under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code are separate and different in nature.
7. In Chandan Kumar Sahoo (supra) also it was held that the proceedings under Section 498A IPC and under Section 12 of the Act are quite different, standing on different footings.
A proceeding under Section 12 of the Act is not a criminal Proceeding even if there are allegations of facts which constitute one or more offences in IPC.

Whereas, proceeding under Section 498A IPC is criminal in nature and the object is to try the perpetrators and punish the guilt while proceeding under the Act is to provide civil remedies to the victims of domestic violence which is not available in the criminal law.
It was also held that standard of proof required in two proceedings are also entirely different.

In civil cases preponderance of probabilities would be sufficient to discharge the onus while in a criminal case the entire burden lies on the prosecution and the proof beyond reasonable doubt has to be given.
Further, a proceeding under the Act is quasi-criminal in nature and not criminal proceeding as under IPC.

Under such Mohd. Kalam & Ors Vs. Smt. Shabnam Taranum Page no.4 of 5.
circumstances door can not be shut to the aggrieved person simply because of identical facts being pleaded in the previous proceeding under Section 498A IPC, which ended in acquittal.

entities.text: Mohd. Kalam & Ors Vs. Smt. Shabnam Taranum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Hence, from the above judgments, it is clear that the acquittal of an offender under Section 498A IPC does not bar a proceeding against him under the Act.

9. Therefore, the arguments of the counsel for the appellants that the acquittal of appellant no.1 and 2 in case FIR No. 734/2016, under Section 406/498A/34 IPC and concealment of this fact by the respondent in her complaint before the Ld. Trial Court, bars the summoning of the appellants, holds no water.
10. Further, in the complaint, there are clear allegations of domestic violence by the appellants and therefore, there are sufficient material on record for proceeding against them.
11. Having discussed as above, this court finds that the impugned order is correct and needs no interference.
Hence, the appeal stands dismissed.
12. Nothing observed herein above, shall, however, be construed as any expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
13. TCR be sent back along with a copy of this order.
File be consigned to record room, as per rules.
(Subhash Kumar Mishra) Additional Sessions Judge-07, South-East, Saket Courts, ND 16.11.2023
